title: Endpoint performance & financial derivation pipeline (per-model / per-tenant)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a robust pipeline that ingests runtime request traces and telemetry and emits an explainable per-endpoint (API endpoint) breakdown of cost and latency attributed to: model variant, tenant, and runtime subsystems (batching, KV cache, kernel selection, IO). Outputs will power Console views, per-tenant billing reconciliations, and regressions alerts. The goal is high fidelity for SLA investigations while keeping compute overhead reasonable for daily rollups.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming pipeline accepts runtime events (trace_id, endpoint, model_variant, tenant_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, batching_metadata, cache_hit) and produces per-endpoint daily & 5-minute rollups
Breakdown includes: model_token_cost, infra_token_cost (GPU time proxy), batching_latency_share, cache_latency_save, and percentage attribution to tenant vs shared overhead
Console API returns breakdowns within 200ms for recent 1h windows and within 1s for 30d queries
Rollups match budgeted chargebacks within 1.5% in synthetic reconciliation tests
Pipeline has schema validation and graceful handling for missing fields (falls back to best-effort attribution)
design_notes: Use hybrid architecture: streaming (Beam) for near-real-time 5m windows + daily batch (Spark) for heavyweight joins and reconciliations
Tag each runtime request with a deterministic attribution token (trace_id + allocation_vector) at ingress to allow deterministic aggregation downstream

Attribution model: first allocate per-token GPU execution time using kernels' runtime cost estimates, then apportion shared infra overhead (router, init time) proportional to tokens or request weight depending on endpoint SLA tier

Tradeoffs considered: finer-grained attribution (per-kernel) yields higher accuracy but requires more runtime instrumentation and cardinality; chosen middle ground instruments batching boundaries and cache hits which capture 85–95% of variance in cost
Privacy: tenant identifiers are pseudonymized in analytics datasets. Full tenant->id mapping only exists in a restricted vault for billing exports
implementation_plan: 1) Define canonical runtime event schema and publish to runtime engineers (tracked in RDOC: /confluence/console-analytics/runtime-event-spec)
2) Implement event producer in runtime (PR# github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/1423) that emits attribution fields
3) Build Beam streaming job that computes 1m and 5m windows, tags cache-hit vs miss, and writes to bigquery_console_realtime.rollups
4) Build daily Spark job to join with pricing catalog and kernel-cost model and write final daily rollups to bigquery_console_aggregates
5) Add REST endpoints in console-backend to serve 1h and 30d aggregations with caching layer
6) Add dashboards and alerts in Grafana for drift between streaming vs batch reconciliations
7) Run two-week parallel validation with synthetic traffic and one customer pilot
testing_plan: Unit tests for attribution math with edge cases (zero-token requests, batched multi-tenant bundles)
Integration tests in staging with synthetic runtime events that vary batching/KV/cache patterns
Backfill reconciliation: compare streaming 5m rollups to batch daily aggregates for 30 days; target <1.5% drift
Load test: simulate 10k rps of runtime events to validate Beam job autoscaling and BigQuery ingestion throughput
Privacy test: ensure exported analytic datasets have tenant pseudonyms and no PII
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal team only, enable on 1 runtime pool, verify stability for 72h
Beta: enable for two pilot customers with opt-in billing exports, collect feedback
GA: expose via Console in 'Cost breakdown' tab and enable daily billing export for enterprise customers
Fallback: if streaming pipeline degraded, show best-effort last-known rollup and mark 'stale' with explanation
